home.first_start_confirm_pad: When it asks to create game data, choose Yes and confirm with ✕ (Cross): {keys} on the keyboard or {pad} on a controller.
home.first_start_confirm: When it asks to create game data, choose Yes and confirm with ✕ (Cross): {keys} on the keyboard.
home.first_start_cancel_first: If a question starts on Cancel or No, press {right} to move to Yes or OK, then confirm.

games.remove_text_linked: This deletes the prepared game files{size}. Your disc image stays where it is, your saves and replays are kept, and you can install the game again later.
games.page_note: Each game keeps its own prepared files, memory card, saves and replays, and reads your disc image where it is. Graphics, display, controls and textures are shared by both.

settings.textures_missing: {path} was not found. The default folder is used.

about.disclaimer: GT4Recomp is an unofficial fan project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Sony Interactive Entertainment or Polyphony Digital.
about.trademarks: Gran Turismo and the Gran Turismo 4 logo are trademarks of Sony Interactive Entertainment Inc. and Polyphony Digital Inc. They are used here only to identify the game. You need your own copy of the game to play.
about.spec2_credit: Gran Turismo 4 Spec II is a mod by TheAdmiester and contributors.
about.contributors: GitHub contributors: thanks to everyone who helped build GT4Recomp on GitHub.
about.contributor_kaezzey: Kaezzey (Niket Shah): started gt4-staticrecomp, the project GT4Recomp grew from.
about.contributor_gustavocanepa: Wise (gustavocanepa): author of gt4-decomp, the game's decompilation that gives GT4Recomp its function names, and a check that refuses repeated GS settings.
about.contributor_julioheroz: Julio Vitor Rufino (JulioHeroZ): racing wheel support, RetroAchievements, and the chosen renderer kept when the launcher updates it.
about.contributor_luanantony: Luan Antony (luanantony): racing wheel integration, DualSense trigger curves, and many fixes and studies; in 1.3.0, the game without a sound device, the GT Auto bubbles that never stopped, clearer messages when the game closes, and the 480p hold.
setting.language.label: Language
setting.language.help: The language of the launcher. Auto follows your Windows language (Portuguese (Brazil) or English); the other two choices always use that language.
setting.renderer.label: Renderer
setting.renderer.help: CoreGS 2.0 is our own renderer and the recommended one: it is part of the game and uses much less processor. GSdx is optional: it is downloaded when you choose it.
setting.vsync.help_coregs20: On keeps motion smooth with no tearing. Off lowers latency and may tear.
settings.gsdx_text: GSdx is not on this PC yet. It is an optional renderer, downloaded from the internet. If you cancel, CoreGS 2.0 stays selected.
settings.gsdx_file_hint: On another network or PC, download the newest gt4-gs-…-windows-x64.zip from github.com/moesuito/gt4recomp-gs/releases, then pick it here.
setting.frame_rate.label: Frame rate (experimental)
setting.frame_rate.help: 60 FPS is the default: in a race, when the PC cannot keep up, the frame rate drops instead of the game slowing down, with the same physics. The 30 FPS mode is for weaker PCs: races draw 30 frames per second. Both are experimental; menus stay at 60.
setting.coregs_sharpening.label: Sharpening (FSR1)
setting.coregs_sharpening.help: AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 1 sharpening of the final picture. Off leaves the picture as the game drew it.
setting.performance_mode.help_coregs20: Faster on weaker PCs. Off draws with full graphics precision. On turns off the night lights, the sun glare and the sheen on the road, draws small effects at lower resolution and stops waiting for some images from the graphics card. Applies the next time you play.
setting.texture_load.label: Load custom textures
setting.texture_load.help: Loads the texture pack from the Textures folder: put the pack's files straight in it. An empty folder changes nothing.
setting.graphics_api.label: API
setting.graphics_api.help: Automatic uses Vulkan when the graphics card supports Vulkan 1.2, otherwise Direct3D 11. Choose Vulkan, Direct3D 12 or Direct3D 11 to force one.
setting.graphics_card.label: Graphics card
setting.graphics_card.help: The graphics card that draws the game. Automatic picks a dedicated card over integrated graphics, then the one with the most video memory.
setting.render_scale.label: Render scale
setting.render_scale.help: How sharp the picture is drawn. 100% draws it at least at your resolution (taken from the Resolution setting on the Display page); 50% is faster and softer, 200% is sharper and needs a much faster GPU. The number next to the slider is the resulting internal resolution.
setting.monitor.label: Monitor
setting.monitor.help: The screen the game opens on. The primary monitor is used until you pick another one.
setting.resolution.label: Resolution
setting.resolution.help: The size of the picture, from the sizes your monitor supports. The shape of the screen follows it: at 16:9 the game is unchanged, other shapes widen or heighten the race view. A size below the monitor's own is drawn at that size and stretched to fill the screen.
setting.fullscreen.label: Fullscreen
setting.fullscreen.help: Start in fullscreen on the chosen monitor (a borderless window that covers it). Alt+Enter or F11 switches while playing.
setting.vsync.label: VSync
setting.vsync.help: On keeps motion smooth with no tearing. Fast and Off lower latency and may tear. Modes the graphics driver lacks are not offered.
setting.performance_hud.label: Performance HUD
setting.performance_hud.help: Shows a panel in the corner while you play: frame rate, frame time with a live graph, and the game's use of the processor, the graphics card and memory.
setting.performance_report.label: Performance report
setting.performance_report.help: Records frame timing while you play for bug reports.
setting.discord_rich_presence.label: Discord Rich Presence
setting.discord_rich_presence.help: Shows that you are playing Gran Turismo 4 or Gran Turismo 4 Spec II in your Discord profile while a game runs. Shows the game name, GT4Recomp and the session time. No mode, track, car, save, account or path is shared. On by default; turn it off to keep your play private.
setting.check_vu_code.label: Check compiled VU code
setting.check_vu_code.help: Compares compiled vector-unit code with the reference while playing. Slower.
setting.l2_deadzone.label: L2 deadzone
setting.r2_deadzone.label: R2 deadzone
setting.l2_curve.label: L2 curve
setting.r2_curve.label: R2 curve
setting.lstick_deadzone.label: Left stick deadzone
setting.rstick_deadzone.label: Right stick deadzone
setting.trigger_deadzone.help: How far the trigger must travel before it counts, in percent of its travel. The pressure the game reads starts above this point.
setting.trigger_curve.help: How the pressure grows with the trigger travel. Linear follows the trigger; quadratic and cubic give finer control at light pressure.
setting.stick_deadzone.help: How far the stick must move from the centre before the game sees it, in percent of its travel. The default is the XInput standard; lower it for a precise pad, raise it for one that drifts.
setup.step_copying_detail: your disc image stays where it is
setup.step_decompressing_detail: the game reads a plain copy; your .chd stays where it is

setup.missing_text: Choose your disc image again to copy the game files. Your saves and settings are kept.
setup.checking_text: This only happens once. Keep GT4Recomp open until it finishes.

setup.choose_text: Choose your Gran Turismo 4 or Gran Turismo 4 Spec II disc image (.iso or .chd). GT4Recomp recognises the game from the disc. This only happens once for each game.
library.saves_note: Each game's marked save is used the next time that game is played.
library.empty_saves_text: Your first save appears here after you save in the game.
library.delete_save_text: The save goes to the Recycle Bin. You can restore it from there.
library.delete_active_save_text: This is your active save. It goes to the Recycle Bin, and the next Play starts a new profile in the game. You can restore it from there.
library.replays_note: All replays are kept. Replays you save in the game appear here.
library.empty_replays_text: Replays you save in the game appear here.
library.delete_replay_text: The replay goes to the Recycle Bin. You can restore it from there.
library.new_save_text_kept: Your current save is kept as {slot}. The next Play starts a new profile in the game.
library.new_save_text_none: There is no active save. The next Play starts a new profile in the game.
controls.title: Controls
controls.tip: Bindings are saved to controls.toml in the GT4Recomp data folder. This game build still uses the built-in mapping; your bindings, trigger and stick settings apply from the next game build.
controls.locked: The controls file was written by a newer GT4Recomp and is kept as it is. Update the launcher to change controls.
controls.connected_many: Connected · {count} controllers, this one is the one the game uses
controls.connect_hint: Connect one, or press a button on it
setting.controller.label: Controller
setting.controller.help: The controller the game reads when several are connected. At every start the launcher selects a connected one: the one you chose last time, or else the first one connected.
controls.controller_unmapped_note: Could not map automatically: {names}. An SDL mapping for it in gamecontrollerdb.txt, in the launcher's config folder, makes it usable.
controls.keyboard_fixed: The keyboard layout is fixed in this build. Switch to Controller to rebind a button.
controls.click_again: Click or tap the button again to rebind it.
controls.not_in_layout: Not in the fixed layout yet
controls.legend_fixed: Fixed keyboard layout, read only. Several keys drive one button.
setting.trigger_full_range.label: Full trigger range
setting.trigger_full_range.help: Throttle and brake follow the whole travel of the triggers in finer steps: about 255 levels instead of the game's own 46 for the throttle and 85 for the brake, still 100% at the end of the travel. Off is the game as it was made.
controls.meter_help: Grey: the trigger now. Blue: the pressure the game reads. Stripes: the deadzone.
controls.capture_text: Press a button or pull a trigger on the controller, or press a key.
controls.capture_foot: B cancels, so it cannot be picked here. To move B, rebind the button that has it and choose Swap.
controls.keys_fixed_capture: Keyboard keys are fixed in this build. Press a controller button, or B to cancel.
controls.file_kept: The controls file is kept as it is (written by a newer GT4Recomp).
controls.no_button_pressed: No button was pressed. Nothing changed.
controls.move_text: Move it: {name} gets {source} and {holder} is left without a {what}.
controls.reset_all_text: Every button, trigger and stick setting goes back to its default. This is saved at once.
controls.reset_all_done: All controls are back to their defaults.
controls.keys_fixed_toast: The keyboard layout is fixed in this build. Switch to Controller to reset a button.
controls.keys_fixed_rebind: The keyboard layout is fixed in this build. Switch to Controller to rebind a button.
controls.svg_label: DualShock 2 controller. Select a button to change what drives it.

setting.fxaa.label: Anti-aliasing
setting.fxaa.help: Smooths jagged edges with a fast filter. It softens fine detail a little. Off by default.
setting.performance_mode.label: Performance Mode
setting.performance_mode.help: Faster on weaker PCs. The game stops waiting for the graphics card to send images back: the car icons next to the gap time can come out blank and the loading screen picture may be missing. The night lights and the sun glare are turned off. Applies the next time you play.
setting.cas_mode.label: Sharpening (CAS)
setting.cas_mode.help: FidelityFX Contrast Adaptive Sharpening. Off leaves the picture as the game drew it.
setting.cas_sharpness.label: Sharpening amount
setting.cas_sharpness.help: How strong the CAS sharpening is. Used when CAS is on.
setting.perf_overlay.label: Performance overlay
setting.perf_overlay.help: Shows GT4Recomp's own overlay while you play (FPS, frame time, CPU and GPU use).
setting.perf_overlay_fps.label: Overlay: FPS
setting.perf_overlay_fps.help: Shows the frame rate in the performance overlay.
setting.launcher_gpu.label: Launcher GPU acceleration
setting.launcher_gpu.help: Off keeps the launcher window without GPU acceleration, after it failed to draw in WebView2. On takes effect at the next start of the launcher.
rust.saves.made_active: It is now the active save, so Play uses it.
rust.saves.went_to_game: It went to {game}, the game this save belongs to.

logs.offer_title: The game stopped with an error

rust.textures.invalid_data_root: That is the launcher's own data folder. Choose the folder that holds the textures instead.
rust.textures.invalid_renderer: That folder belongs to the renderer and is replaced when it updates. Choose another folder.
setting.update_channel.label: Channel
setting.update_channel.help: Stable gets the normal releases. Beta also gets the release candidates, to try new features early. Going back to Stable never installs an older version by itself.
versions.label: Version
versions.help: Pick the GT4Recomp version to install. The list is read from GitHub each time this page opens. Stable lists the normal releases; Beta lists the release candidates.
versions.older_note: Older versions are not listed: they cannot read this version's data.
versions.only_installed: There is no other version on this channel yet. Versions older than 1.3.0-rc5 are not listed: they cannot read this version's data.
versions.nothing_newer: You are on a newer version than any {channel} release; {channel} updates resume when a newer release ships.
versions.confirm_text: GT4Recomp downloads version {version}, checks it, installs it and closes. Start it again afterwards. Your settings and saves are kept.
versions.downgrade_text: You are on {installed}. Version {version} is older.
versions.downgrade_warning: Going back to an older version can break settings, saves or other data. Back up your saves first (Saves > Export, or the saves folder).
rust.update.versions_failed: Could not read the version list ({reason}). Your current version stays.
ra.title: Achievements
ra.subtitle: Sign in with your RetroAchievements account to unlock achievements in-game and record them on retroachievements.org.
ra.relogin_required_desc: Your saved session cannot be unlocked on this Windows account or PC. Sign in again to reconnect your account.
ra.migration_failed_desc: Your saved credentials could not be protected on this PC. Sign in again to save a protected session.
ra.save_failed_desc: Your RetroAchievements settings could not be saved to disk. Check file permissions or disk space.
ra.opt_enabled_help: Starts a RetroAchievements session when the game launches, evaluates PS2 memory triggers each frame, shows on-screen achievement popups, and submits unlocks to retroachievements.org.
ra.opt_hardcore_help: Earns Hardcore points and mastery badges on RetroAchievements.
ra.opt_encore_help: Allows achievements you have already unlocked to trigger again during this session.
ra.modal_text: Your password is sent once over HTTPS to retroachievements.org to obtain an API token. Only your username and protected token are stored on this PC.
ra.err_save_migration: Cannot change options: your existing login credentials could not be protected. Please sign in again.
ra.err_save_failed: Failed to save RetroAchievements settings. Check file permissions or disk space.
ra.sign_out_text: Your stored API token will be removed from this PC.
ra.unsupported_title: RetroAchievements is not available for Gran Turismo 4 Spec II
ra.unsupported_desc: Achievements are supported only on the original Gran Turismo 4 (v2.00) release. You can switch to Gran Turismo 4 in the Games menu to view and unlock achievements.
